selection_framework.high_temperature_strength: Refractory-metal selection is governed by temperature, time, environment and microstructure rather than room-temperature strength alone.
selection_framework.ductile_brittle_transition: Several refractory metals can show strong temperature-dependent ductility; transition behaviour must be considered for handling, assembly and low-temperature service.
selection_framework.creep: Long-duration high-temperature exposure requires creep/rupture evidence matched to grade and processing route.
selection_framework.fracture: Purity, grain size, fabrication history and environmental contamination can materially influence fracture behaviour.
selection_framework.density: Density can be a major system-level discriminator, particularly for aerospace and moving components.
selection_framework.thermal: Thermal conductivity and CTE can strongly influence thermal gradients, joint loads and transient response.

rule: Refractory-metal data must retain environment and processing condition; air-exposed high-temperature performance cannot be inferred from vacuum/inert-environment data.
